messages.body_plain:

Regards

messages.subject: Annotate a list of trees with user annotations
messages.subject_clean: Annotate a list of trees with user annotations
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a list of trees, stored under a multiphylo object. Each tree is from different part of the genome and all trees have the same taxa, thus tip names.
What I would like to do is to color the tips of my trees according to an external annotation.
I know that ggtree has %<+% that allow attaching an annotation to a tree. Is there a way to work around to make this work with a multiphylo object so that I can visualize them all at once with facet_wrap. Otherwise, I will have to do this one by one and assembling them à posteriori, which will require much more manipulation.

Thank you very much in advance.

messages.subject: Re: Annotate a list of trees with user annotations
messages.subject_clean: Annotate a list of trees with user annotations
messages.body_plain:
In this case, you don’t need to attach external data to the tree object.

Just visualize the tree and color the tip by tip label, than use scale_color_manual to set the colors.

messages.subject: Problem plotting with revts() and geom_nodelab()
messages.subject_clean: Problem plotting with revts() and geom_nodelab()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am having an issue plotting nodelabels. Everything works fine until I reverse the x axis, then the nodelabels plot next to the tree, almost like a facet.

Example:

x <- read.beast("/Applications/FigTree/influenza.tree")
x1 <- ggtree(x) + theme_tree2()
x2 <- revts(x1)
x3 <- x2 + scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(-13:0), labels=abs(-13:0))
x3

Then once I add the node labels:

x4 <- x3 + geom_nodelab(aes(x=branch, label=round(posterior, 2)))
x4

I have tried this in different orders (node labels first, then revts()) but I can't figure it out.

Any ideas?

Thanks you!
Jon

messages.subject: geom_segment and plot resolution
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would like to plot a tree with lines connecting branches from different clades.

I can do this with geom_segment, but the resolution of the lines seems poor when compared to geom_taxalink.

Is there a way to improve the resolution of lines in geom_segment or more intelligent way of drawing lines between branches?

I have attached example code and pdfs of plots

Cheers
Ollie

library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(123)
tree <- rtree(30)

# nodes to connect
n1 <- MRCA(tree, tip = c("t18", "t13"))
n2 <- MRCA(tree, tip = c("t2", "t4"))
n3 <- MRCA(tree, tip = c("t29", "t16"))

# create ggtree object
p <- ggtree(tree, branch.length = "none")

# get node info from ggtree object
N1 <- p$data[n1,]
N2 <- p$data[n2,]
N3 <- p$data[n3,]

# plot tree with lines connecting branches
pdf(file = "test-segment.pdf", height = 5, width = 7)
p +
  geom_tiplab() +
  geom_segment2(aes(x = N1$x-0.6, xend = N2$x-0.6, y = N1$y, yend = N2$y), colour = "red", size = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both")) +
  geom_segment2(aes(x = N1$x-0.4, xend = N3$x-0.4, y = N1$y, yend = N3$y), colour = "red", size = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both"))
dev.off()

# plot tree with geom_taxalink for comparison
pdf(file = "test-taxalink.pdf", height = 5, width = 7)
p +
  geom_tiplab() +
  geom_taxalink(n1, n2, colour = "red", curvature = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both")) +
  geom_taxalink(n1, n3, colour = "red", curvature = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both"))
dev.off()
